scope.summary: Build the genital config panel per Section 13.27 GUI clauses: cock/pussy/anus channel sliders at the same grain as every other region — no special-casing, no extra friction — plus erection state (continuum + rigid/floppy), gape dials including the extreme range, and the arousal controller, all labeled in direct production language (MT-601 surface; REQ-030..032, PREQ-013).
acceptance_criteria: Penis channels (length/girth/curve/taper, glans, foreskin continuum, vein intensity, scrotum), vulva channels (labia size/shape/spread, clit, gape incl. extreme, canal depth), and anus channels render as standard sliders identical in grain and interaction to any body region — no special confirmation dialogs, no segregated mode.
Erection continuum slider plus rigid|floppy state toggle and gape dials drive the same channel ops as configure_genitals (asserted equivalence).
The arousal controller slider live-drives flush/engorgement/wetness/nipple-erection preview in the viewport (MT-559 hook).
Labels use direct language (cock, pussy, gape, erection) matching the channel registry ids; no euphemistic renaming layer exists.
All controls carry stable author_ids; Argus sets an erection state and captures the result headlessly; futa configs show both modules' panels concurrently without conflict.

The exact TailorSurfaceDescriptor row MT-632 enumerates every route, pane, control author_id, dynamic entity-key rule, action, state, help anchor, permission, undo policy, receipt, and command binding; wildcard-only evidence is rejected.

Applicable blank, loading, populated, stale/conflict, cancelled, failed, retry, permission, keyboard/focus, narrow/4K/DPI, overlap/clipping, and no-focus-steal states are covered by the registry-derived Argus matrix.

The panel exposes every MT-730/MT-731 vulva, penis, scrotum, erection, foreskin, asymmetry, pigmentation, wetness, and interior channel with searchable grouping, authored/effective values, shape-family presets, reference comparison, and exact stable IDs.
scope.risk_if_missed: Special-casing or euphemizing the primary production surface adds exactly the friction and second-class treatment that pushed this content into Daz's aftermarket-graft ghetto — the anti-pattern BodyKit is designed against.

surfaces: BodyKit genital configuration and arousal panel

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit workspace and controls

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: BodyKit GUI must expose or integrate the geometry/morph, joint, weight/rigidity, transfer, skin/material, interlink, Jobs, Problems, history, recovery, and shared-world contracts.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.
Use PostgreSQL RLS/FORCE RLS and ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; UI filtering is never the security boundary.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
